subject: Film & Cinema
title: Adapting Books to Screen
description: A fast breakdown of Adapting Books to Screen for builders.

hook.text: Fans say 'the book was better' so often it's become a cliché. They're usually right.

buildup.text: Novels live in internal thought. Films live in external action and visual storytelling.

discovery.text: Successful adaptations capture the spirit of a book, not every plot detail.

twist.text: The Shining infuriated Stephen King but became one of the greatest horror films ever.

climax.text: Adaptation is translation — the languages of page and screen are fundamentally different.

punchline.text: Faithful means capturing the soul, not the words.

quiz.question: What is the key challenge in adapting a novel to film?
options: Translating internal thoughts into visual storytelling
Making the film longer than the book
